appraisal_events.evidence: les idées qu'il exposait jadis sur l'art de la guerre... s'étaient souvent et, en somme, sur un grand nombre de points trouvées vérifiées par la dernière guerre; Gilberte parlait de lui sur un ton déférent, comme si c'eût été un être supérieur; a critic (M. Henry Bidou) independently echoes almost verbatim the analytic framework Robert had used.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator and Gilberte together affirm that Robert's wartime strategic ideas were subsequently borne out by real events and independently echoed by a respected military critic, posthumously elevating his intellectual standing.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle répétait d'un air exalté et d'une voix de ferraille que lui faisait son râtelier... elle était décidée à «participer», à «faire clan», bien qu'elle fût mi-amusé, mi-s'excusant de ne pouvoir soutenir la gaîté longtemps.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's description undercuts her performed enthusiasm by tying her voice to her dentures and her insistence on joining the young company to a visible inability to sustain the gaiety, producing a gently mocking portrait of strained, aging sociability.

status_effects.explanation: His once-private military theorizing is shown to have anticipated real historical developments and to align with expert critical analysis, posthumously enhancing his intellectual reputation.

The narrator extends and builds on Robert's framing of war as a human, narrative-like phenomenon rather than pure strategy, implicitly crediting Robert's perceptiveness as the starting point for his own reflection.
The ironic emphasis on her altered voice and her strained, repetitive effort to seem youthfully sociable locally lowers her standing, even though the tone remains gentle rather than harsh.

ambiguities: The bare form 'princesse de Guermantes' in this Bal de têtes scene is flagged by the reference sheet as genuinely ambiguous between the original princesse de Guermantes (Marie-Gilbert) and Mme Verdurin, who later holds the same title by remarriage. The speaker's repeated 'nous ferons clan' echoes the Verdurins' signature salon idiom, suggesting this may in fact be Mme Verdurin, but per registry policy the identity is left unresolved rather than guessed.
